title: Degree selection from another map raised total link recovery in two passive adult worm models
abstract: We tested cell selection for direct electrical link inference in two partial adult C. elegans maps. Each passive model had 180 cells, equal white current noise and count-based conductance. Selecting 90 cells by degree in the other map recovered 52.67% and 55.41% of all model links from exact covariance, versus random-mask means of 24.66% and 24.73%. Most of this gain came from observing more links. An exploratory test with 1,000 independent Gaussian snapshots gave mean recovery of 41.54% and 41.17%, versus 20.49% and 19.17% for random selection. Other-map precision was slightly lower at that sample size. At 100 samples all strategies had poor precision. The benchmark assumes a known observed link count, passive dynamics and independent samples. Two incomplete maps and no measured activity limit biological use. Original code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction. External anatomical records are excluded.
